system_description.narrative_title: Economic/financial offensive on Iran destabilizes energy markets and regional security
system_description.narrative_summary: News cluster around a coordinated U.S.-led economic campaign (sanctions, secondary measures and financial pressure) against Iran, and allied private initiatives, is the single dominant narrative. That campaign is propagating through open channels — oil and refined fuels flows, tanker logistics, insurance and ports, regional proxy activity and cyber operations — producing market shocks, refinery stress and regional escalations that feed back into policy and commercial decisions. The system is open: information, capital, commodities and force cross the boundary and trigger reactive countermeasures (Iranian threats, Gulf state actions, third‑party buyers like China) that amplify uncertainty.
system_description.scope: Diplomatic and financial coercion targeting Iran; U.S. and allied sanction policy and secondary measures; Gulf maritime transit (Strait of Hormuz) and tanker logistics; global crude and refined product markets and refineries; regional proxy attacks and cyber operations; responses by China, Gulf states, Europe and energy firms.
system_description.super_system: The global geopolitical‑economic and energy security system (interconnected international politics, finance, energy markets and maritime trade).
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil & refining markets (prices, inventories, refinery margins, SPRs)
International financial sanctions & payment infrastructure (secondary sanctions, banking, insurance)
Middle East regional security architecture (state and proxy military/cyber actions, Gulf politics)
Maritime shipping, tankers and insurance markets
evidence_headlines: Donald Trump announces fresh ‘economic warfare’ on Iran
Bessent Launches ‘Operation Economic Outcast’ to Isolate and Squeeze Iran
U.S. to unveil 'greatest financial offensive' against Iran as Tehran threatens ship seizures
Demand for tankers soars as Gulf oil producers search for ways to export cargoes
Western oil refinery closures set to continue despite war shock
UAE suspends trade with Iran after saying it fired missiles at Gulf state

variables.name: Financial coercion level
variables.description: Aggregate intensity of economic and financial pressure tools (sanctions, asset restrictions, payment constraints) applied against the target economy.

variables.name: Sanction scope coverage
variables.description: Breadth of sanction measures across geographic regions and economic sectors that affect trade and finance channels.

variables.name: Secondary pressure effectiveness
variables.description: Effectiveness of extraterritorial/secondary measures in altering third‑party commercial and financial behavior toward the target.

variables.name: Trade finance availability
variables.description: Accessibility and capacity of banking, letters of credit, correspondent networks and other payment instruments that enable cross‑border trade in affected commodities.

variables.name: Crude throughput rate
variables.description: Rate of crude oil volume transiting key maritime chokepoints and export routes per unit time.

variables.name: Refined product supply balance
variables.description: Net balance between available refined fuels (gasoline, diesel, jet) and regional demand, expressed as surplus or deficit.

variables.name: Tanker capacity availability
variables.description: Available seaborne transport capacity for crude and refined product shipments relative to logistical demand.

variables.name: Marine insurance cost
variables.description: Average premiums and war‑risk surcharges charged to insure maritime shipments through contested routes.

variables.name: Refinery utilization rate
variables.description: Percentage of installed refinery processing capacity that is operational and processing feedstock at a given time.

variables.name: Regional military escalation
variables.description: Intensity and tempo of conventional and irregular military actions in the region that affect security of trade and infrastructure.

variables.name: Proxy attack frequency
variables.description: Rate at which proxy or irregular forces carry out attacks against infrastructure, shipping, or military assets in the operational theater.

variables.name: Cyber disruption incidence
variables.description: Frequency and severity of cyber operations that disrupt energy infrastructure, logistics, or trade‑support systems.

variables.name: Third‑party buyer demand
variables.description: Level of demand from non‑sanctioning or neutral buyers for the target's commodity exports.

variables.name: Market price volatility
variables.description: Degree of short‑term variability and uncertainty in commodity and refined product prices perceived by market participants.

variables.name: Financial market liquidity
variables.description: Depth and ease with which financial assets and trade settlements can be transacted without large price impacts in markets relevant to the campaign.

variables.name: Coalition policy cohesion
variables.description: Degree of alignment and coordination among relevant governments and policy actors in designing and enforcing collective measures.

catalysts.title: U.S. announces major financial offensive on Iran
catalysts.description: Imminent U.S. announcement of a broad, coordinated sanctions/financial campaign aimed at isolating Iran and pressuring partners to cut economic ties.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Donald Trump announces fresh ‘economic warfare’ on Iran'; 'U.S. to unveil 'greatest financial offensive''.

catalysts.title: U.S. broadens scope of secondary sanctions
catalysts.description: U.S. Treasury expands extraterritorial measures targeting third‑party banks, shippers and trading partners to choke Iran's commerce.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'US Treasury to broaden scope of secondary sanctions on Iran, source says'.

catalysts.title: China's response: shielding or supply‑shift
catalysts.description: China signals protection of its economic rights and adjusts crude sourcing — either shielding Iran or shifting imports outside the Gulf.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'China vows to protect its rights as US readies Iran sanction'; 'Looming US sanctions put China oil buying in spotlight'.

catalysts.title: Iran tightens Strait of Hormuz transit rules
catalysts.description: Iran threatens fines, detention and tighter transit rules for vessels, reducing flows and raising seizure risk through the Strait of Hormuz.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Iran threatens 46 ships in Strait of Hormuz transit crackdown'; 'Iran warns vessels... fines, detention'.

catalysts.title: Houthis/other proxies escalate attacks
catalysts.description: Ongoing Houthi strikes and proxy actions against shipping and regional targets continue, raising attack frequency and insurance costs.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Houthis escalate campaign against Saudi Arabia'; 'Yemen's Houthis say they attacked ship off Saudi Arabia's Yanbu'.

catalysts.title: Surge in tanker demand and vessel stacking
catalysts.description: Producers and traders increase reliance on tankers to reroute, store or bypass routes, creating capacity shortages and logistical backlogs.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Demand for tankers soars'; 'Tankers stack up as Venezuela sells oil faster than its ports can handle'.

catalysts.title: State‑backed war insurance talks in Gulf
catalysts.description: Gulf states consider state‑supported war‑risk insurance to stabilise shipping costs and encourage continued exports amid rising premiums.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Saudi Arabia holds talks over state-backed war insurance as costs jump'.

catalysts.title: Iran‑linked cyberattacks on energy firms
catalysts.description: Reported Iran‑linked cyber intrusions against UK energy assets continue, prompting increased alerts and potential operational disruptions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Small UK power generator shut down after cyberattack linked to Iran'; 'UK energy companies on alert after ‘Iran-linked hackers’'.

catalysts.title: Continuing Western refinery closures and stress
catalysts.description: Ongoing structural refinery closures in the West reduce refining capacity, tightening refined product balances as crude disruptions persist.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Western oil refinery closures set to continue'; 'The Hormuz crude volume debate masks the real shortage of refined fuels'.
